source: Original converted descriptions and schemas. S replacement text was not an input to the cue wording.
editor: same editor, after S was specified
review_question: Could both descriptions be true of the same request, and if so, does this cue still help the reader choose?

coverage.note: These denominators are the sealed tranche, not the 840. Coverage is not cue efficiency. Shorter wording is not the success criterion.

cases.case_reason: Three fetch tools on one country. The two city facts share an action and a resource. Population is a different returned fact, so its rival is the earlier city tool.

tools.cue: Unlike country_info_capital, which fetches the capital city, this fetches the largest city.

rival.axis: which city fact of the country is fetched
rival.why_confusable: Both fetch a city of a specified country. A request that only says the country's city can be read as either.
rival.why_this_rival: Capital is the same action on the same resource, a city of the country. Population returns a count, so it is not the closer rival.
rejected: country_info_population returns a count, not a city.

same_request.note: A request that says capital or largest city makes only one description true. A request that only says the country's city can be read as either, and the cue names which city fact.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike country_info_largest_city, which fetches the largest city, this fetches the capital city.

rival.axis: which city fact of the country is fetched
rival.why_confusable: Both fetch a city of a specified country.
rival.why_this_rival: Largest city is the other city fact. Population is a count.
rejected: country_info_population is a different returned fact.

same_request.note: The two city descriptions are not included in each other. The cue names the city fact a vague request left open.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike country_info_largest_city, which fetches the largest city, this fetches the current population.

rival.axis: whether the returned country fact is a city or the current population
rival.why_confusable: All three tools fetch a fact about a specified country. An underspecified country request can be offered to any of them.
rival.why_this_rival: The two city tools are the same kind of alternative to a population count. Catalogue order selects the earlier city tool.
rejected: Naming both city tools in one cue.
Using country_info_capital, which is the later city tool.

same_request.note: A request for the population does not make the largest-city description true. A request that only names the country can be read as either, and the cue names the returned fact. Current stays in the cue because the source says current population.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: Both tools take an initial speed, an acceleration, and a time. The selection axis is the quantity they return.

rival.why_confusable: Both calculate a straight-line motion quantity from initial speed, acceleration, and time.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool, and it states the other quantity.
rejected: The rounding argument is shared machinery, not the selection axis.

same_request.note: A request that only says the object accelerated for a time can be read as asking for either quantity. A request that names displacement does not make the final-speed description true.

tools.cue: Unlike kinematics_calculate_displacement, which calculates displacement, this calculates the final speed.

rival.axis: which kinematic quantity is calculated
rival.why_confusable: Both calculate a straight-line motion quantity from initial speed, acceleration, and time.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool.
rejected: Do not treat float versus integer parameter types as the reason to choose a tool.

same_request.note: The descriptions name different quantities. The cue repeats that difference and does not say either tool rejects a duration.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: All three read one grade dictionary. Standard deviation and average are the same action, a statistic over the scores. The highest-score tool finds a subject instead.

tools.cue: Unlike calculate_average, which calculates the average grade, this calculates the standard deviation.

rival.axis: which statistic of the scores is calculated
rival.why_confusable: Both calculate a statistic from the same kind of subject-to-score dictionary for one student.
rival.why_this_rival: Average is the same action, a summary statistic. Finding the subject with the highest score is a different action.
rejected: highest_grade returns a subject, not a statistic.

same_request.note: A request to summarize the scores can be read as either statistic. The descriptions are not included in each other: an average is not a standard deviation.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike calculate_standard_deviation, which calculates the standard deviation, this calculates the average grade.

rival.axis: which statistic of the scores is calculated
rival.why_confusable: Both calculate a statistic from the same kind of grade dictionary.
rival.why_this_rival: Standard deviation is the same action. The subject-finding tool is a different action.
rejected: highest_grade is a different action.

same_request.note: A request for the student's overall grade can be read as the average. The cue names that statistic against the spread.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike calculate_standard_deviation, which calculates the standard deviation, this finds the subject with the highest score.

rival.axis: whether the result is a statistic or the subject with the highest score
rival.why_confusable: All three read the same grade dictionary. A request about how the student did can be offered to a statistic or to the top subject.
rival.why_this_rival: Both statistics are the same kind of alternative to finding a subject. Catalogue order selects the earlier statistic.
rejected: Naming both statistics in one cue.
Using calculate_average, which is the later statistic.

same_request.note: A request for the strongest subject does not make the standard-deviation description true. A vague request about the scores can be read as either, and the cue names a subject rather than a spread.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: Quadratic roots, an RGB-to-hex conversion, and reversing a string do not share an action or a resource.

tools.no_cue_reason: Solves a quadratic equation. Neither an RGB conversion nor string reversal documents a shared selection axis with that equation.
Converts RGB values to a hexadecimal color. Quadratic roots and string reversal are not color conversions.
Reverses a string. Quadratic roots and an RGB conversion are not string operations on the same resource.

cases.case_reason: Both tools take a single-variable function. One calculates a derivative. The other calculates a definite integral.

tools.cue: Unlike calculate_integral, which calculates the definite integral, this calculates the derivative.

rival.axis: whether the operation is a derivative or a definite integral
rival.why_confusable: Both operate on a single-variable function. A request that only says to do the calculus can be read as either.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool, and the function descriptions name the two operations.
rejected: Do not contrast the class word calculus. A derivative is not a definite integral, and the cue names the operation.

same_request.note: A request for the derivative does not make the definite-integral description true. A request that only names the function can be read as either. The cue uses the operation, not a nested class label.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike calculate_derivative, which calculates the derivative, this calculates the definite integral.

rival.axis: whether the operation is a definite integral or a derivative
rival.why_confusable: Both operate on a single-variable function.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool.
rejected: The bounds versus an x value follow the operation. They are not a second cue.

same_request.note: Definite integral is the source's own qualifier. The cue keeps it so the contrast is not any integral against any derivative.

rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool.

rival.why_confusable: Both calculate interest from an initial amount, an annual rate, and a time in years.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool, and the function descriptions name the two interest types.
rejected: The compounding frequency n is an argument of compound interest, not a contrast that simple interest lacks a rate.

same_request.note: A request that only says interest can be read as either type. Compound and simple are alternate types, not a class and a subclass. The cue names the type.
